assistant-chat.onboarding.card.title: Set up Klacks
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.title: Let's start with the display name of Klacks. This name appears in the browser title, the header and on reports — typically your company or organization name. Everything we configure in this tour can be found later via the gear icon in the left navigation — I'm making it pulse for a moment.
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.brandi: Right here on the same card you can also upload your app icon (.ico or .png) and your logo (.png). The icon appears in the browser tab, the logo in the header and on reports. Both are file uploads directly on the card — upload the files there, not here in the chat.
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.addres: Now the address of your office or headquarters. It appears as the sender address on reports and exports and serves as my default location, for example for the weather in my greeting. On the same card you also set the Global Calendar — your company-wide default public-holiday calendar (country/canton); individual contracts or groups can override it later. You can change both any time via the gear icon (Settings → sender address).
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.defaul: Next, the default language of your installation — it serves as the fallback wherever no personal language choice exists.
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.llm-pr: That's me :) So that I can answer and execute actions, you need to activate an AI provider here and enter its API key (e.g. Anthropic, OpenAI or Groq) — without an active key I stay silent. Deliberately enter API keys here on the card, not in the chat. You can store several providers and pick the default model.
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.llm-sy: Now let's sync the model list of your activated providers. Click the refresh button (the circular-arrow icon) at the top right of this card — I've highlighted it for a moment. The sync runs in the background and can take a moment when there are new models; the result then shows up as an entry here in the log.
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.llm-mo: Now let's pick the right model: I check every stored model for tool-calling reliability and context window, enable the ones that qualify, and suggest the best one as default — you can still choose yourself at any time. Tip: storing several providers pays off, because different tasks need different strengths — the Holistic Harmonizer, for example, needs image capability, while transcription mostly needs speed.
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.harmon: The Holistic Harmonizer smooths and checks your shift schedule with LLM support — it looks at the plan as a whole and proposes corrections. Here you pick its LLM model and can run a one-click check of which models answer reliably and fast enough. You'll use it later in the schedule (calendar icon in the navigation) via the assistant menu in the header.
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.calend: Reminder: further down on this card you already set your company-wide default public-holiday calendar — the Global Calendar field. It drives surcharges, display and plannability in the schedule, which you'll find via the calendar icon in the left navigation. For individual contracts or groups you can later assign a different calendar — the bundles for that are managed under Settings → Calendar Selection.
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.users: Create the user accounts for your team here — every person working with Klacks needs their own login with a suitable role (administrator or restricted). You can add more accounts or change permissions at any time. You always reach this administration via the gear icon → user administration.
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.group-: Here you define per user which groups (teams, sites, areas) they may see — so everyone only sees their own areas and the lists stay tidy. You create the groups themselves via the groups icon in the left navigation — it is flashing right now. Tip: create groups first, then assign visibilities here.
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.identi: Optional: connect an external identity provider (LDAP, Active Directory, OAuth2/OpenID Connect) for single sign-on — your team then logs in with their existing company credentials. Be careful with changes: a misconfigured provider can lock people out. If you don't use one, simply leave the list empty and skip this station.
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.schedu: These are the scheduling defaults: standard working days, hour targets, rest times and similar rules that the schedule and the planning assistants use as their baseline. They take effect directly in the schedule — open it via the calendar icon in the navigation (pulsing right now). You can adjust these values at any time.
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.weeken: These are the scheduling defaults: standard working days, hour targets, rest times and similar rules that the schedule and the planning assistants use as their baseline — including the weekend days and week start, which drive the weekend surcharges (WE1/WE2/WE3). A region-setup.json may already have prefilled these values during installation — take a moment to check that they match your region. They take effect directly in the schedule — open it via the calendar icon in the navigation (pulsing right now). You can adjust all these values at any time.
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.employ: This is the address and people management — the heart of your master data: employees, customers and externals with addresses, contact details, contracts, group membership and qualifications. I just opened it for you; you reach it any time via the people icon in the navigation, pulsing right now. Create your team here after the tour — or simply tell me (»create an employee …«) and I will take care of it.
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.shifts: Here you define the shifts (shift templates): working hours, weekdays, required headcount and required qualifications. Shifts are the building blocks from which the schedule and the planning assistants construct the duty roster — without defined shifts the schedule stays empty. You reach them via the shifts icon in the navigation, flashing right now.
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.availa: In the availability view you record when employees are available for duty and when they are not — per day and hour. The planning assistants and I take this into account when staffing shifts and proposing replacements. You find the view behind the availability icon in the navigation (pulsing right now).
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.period: Period closing is your month-end workplace: approve individual days, close the period and seal it — sealed data is the binding basis for evaluations and exports. As an admin you can also reopen a period when needed. You reach it via the closing icon in the navigation, lighting up right now.
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.absenc: Here you define the absence types of your business — vacation, illness, accident, training and so on, each with a color and short code. These types are then available in the absence planner: the Gantt icon in the left navigation, flashing right now. Well-defined absence types make the annual overview readable at a glance.
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.holida: The holiday rules define which days count as public holidays and how they are calculated — fixed dates like August 1st or movable ones like Easter. They complement the selected calendar and apply everywhere in the schedule: surcharges, display and the planning assistants. You find the schedule behind the calendar icon in the navigation.
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.email: So that Klacks can send e-mails — for example sending schedules to employees — fill in the SMTP fields here and verify them right away with the test button. For receiving e-mail, e.g. for the analysis features and incoming applications, additionally configure the IMAP card just below. Incoming mail lands in the inbox: the letter icon in the navigation, lighting up right now.
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.klacks: Here you fine-tune me: language and voice for speech input (STT) and speech output (TTS), the silence threshold for recording and barge-in (interrupting me while I speak). On the autonomy card you define how much I may do without asking back, and on the personality card how I come across.
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.securi: One important thing to finish: the default admin account (admin@test.com) has a publicly known password. Change it now — or create your own admin account and deactivate the seed account. Until then, anyone can sign in with the default credentials.
assistant-chat.onboarding.explain.plugin: Finally: activate optional feature plugins here — for example messaging (Telegram integration) or additional language packs. Plugins extend Klacks modularly; whatever you don't need stays off and keeps the interface lean. That completes the setup — you can find everything else any time via the gear icon in the navigation. 🎉

assistant-chat.onboarding.ask.default-la: Which default language should the installation use? Enter a language code (de, en, fr, it or an installed plugin language). Invalid values fall back to en on the server.
assistant-chat.onboarding.tour.completed: That's it – Klacks is ready to go! You can find all settings anytime under Settings. 🎉
assistant-chat.onboarding.llm.offline: By the way: Klacksy is still offline because no LLM is set up yet. The tour works anyway – it will take you to the LLM setup in a moment.
assistant-chat.onboarding.llm.online: Klacksy is now online and can answer freely and accompany you through the rest of the tour. 🎉
assistant-chat.onboarding.llm.still-offl: No LLM active yet – you can set this up later at any time in the settings. The tour continues as normal.
assistant-chat.onboarding.llm.free-provi:
Tip: There are free providers to get you started – grab a key, paste it on the card and enable the provider:
- [Cerebras](https://cloud.cerebras.ai) – high free limits, works well for Klacksy, preset available
- [Mistral](https://console.mistral.ai/api-keys) – generous free tier, preset available
- [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/settings/keys) – one key for many models
- [Groq](https://console.groq.com/keys) – very fast, but a small per-minute quota (often too tight for chat)
All available without a credit card.

assistant-chat.welcome.content:
👋 Hi! I'm Klacksy, your assistant. I can help you:

• Create employees
• Search for people
• Manage contracts

You can speak to me or just type. Try: "Create employee Max Muster"

legal.privacy.title: Privacy Policy
legal.privacy.content:
1. Data Controller

The data controller within the meaning of the GDPR is the operator of this Klacks instance. Please refer to the Legal Notice for the controller's contact details.

2. Data Collected and Processed

2.1 User Account

A user account is required to use the application. The following data is processed: email address, password (as a cryptographic hash), first and last name, and the assigned user role. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR (performance of a contract).

2.2 Employee and Client Data

For workforce planning, the following data is processed: name, address, contact details (email, phone), date of birth, gender, profile picture, and GPS coordinates of the address. Contact data is stored encrypted in the database. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR (performance of a contract) or Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (legitimate interest in workforce scheduling).

2.3 Schedules and Absences

Working time data, shift assignments, breaks, expenses, and absences are processed for workforce planning purposes. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR.

3. Data Transfers to Third Parties

Depending on the instance configuration, the following external services may be used:

ServicePurposeData TransferredProvider
OpenStreetMapMap displayIP address, map viewportOpenStreetMap Foundation, UK
NominatimAddress geocodingAddress dataOpenStreetMap Foundation, UK
OpenRouteServiceRoute optimizationGPS coordinates (anonymized)HeiGIT gGmbH, Germany
DeepLText translationTexts to be translatedDeepL SE, Germany
AI AssistantChatbot functionalityChat history, planning dataDepending on configuration (e.g. OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek)
LDAP / OAuth2AuthenticationLogin credentialsDepending on configuration
SMTP / IMAPEmail sending and receivingEmail content, sender, recipientDepending on configuration

These services are used on the basis of Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (legitimate interest in application functionality). Services that are not configured will not be contacted.

4. Browser Storage

The application uses browser storage (LocalStorage) for the following purposes:

  • Authentication: JWT token, refresh token, and token expiry to maintain the session
  • User preferences: Language selection and UI preferences (e.g. column widths)

No third-party tracking cookies or analytics tools are used.

5. Data Storage and Deletion

All data is stored in a PostgreSQL database managed by the operator of this instance.

When records are deleted, a soft-delete marker is initially set. After the configured retention period expires, the data is automatically and irrevocably physically deleted. The retention period can be set by the administrator in the settings.

6. Data Security

Communication between browser and server is exclusively via HTTPS (TLS encryption). Passwords are stored only as cryptographic hashes. Contact data (email, phone) is stored encrypted in the database. Real-time communication (WebSocket/SignalR) is also secured by JWT token authentication.

7. Your Rights

Under the GDPR, you have the following rights:

  • Right of access (Art. 15 GDPR): You may request information about your stored personal data.
  • Right to rectification (Art. 16 GDPR): You may request the correction of inaccurate data.
  • Right to erasure (Art. 17 GDPR): You may request the deletion of your data, provided no legal retention obligations apply.
  • Right to restriction of processing (Art. 18 GDPR)
  • Right to data portability (Art. 20 GDPR)
  • Right to object (Art. 21 GDPR): You may object to the processing of your data.
  • Right to lodge a complaint: You have the right to lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority.

To exercise your rights, please contact the controller listed in the Legal Notice.

8. Changes

This privacy policy may be updated by the operator at any time. The current version is always available on this page.
